I created the seam file `apps/api/src/image-digest.ts`. It exports a single function, `resolveImageDigest(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): Promise<string | undefined>`, with the `async` signature the spec gives. Its body is just `throw new Error("not implemented");`, and its doc comment repeats the spec's rules: it reads `IMAGE_DIGEST` once when called, trims whitespace, accepts only `sha256:` plus 64 lowercase hex characters, otherwise resolves to `undefined`, never throws or rejects, never changes `env`, and keeps no cache.

I left out a few things on purpose:
- **No exported constants:** the spec says the module exports nothing else. `DIGEST_A` and `DIGEST_B` are test fixtures, and the spec explicitly rules out exporting the pattern or the variable name.
- **No error types:** the spec says the function never fails.
- **No other files changed:** `env.ts`, `routes.ts` and the shared types are untouched, as the spec requires.

`npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` compiles with no errors, and all 129 existing tests pass, the same as before.

Added: resolveImageDigest

public.finalText:
I wrote the test suite in `apps/api/test/image-digest.test.ts`. It type-checks with no errors under `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`. When run, 40 tests fail with `not implemented`, as expected. The other 4 already pass: the `[happy-6]` and `[happy-7]` tests check that `parseEnv` and `GET /version` work as before, so they don't need the new code. I changed no other files.

**What's covered:** every one of the 16 scenarios has a happy-path test and at least one boundary test. For the scenario outlines, every example row in the spec gets its own test. Each test name starts with its scenario key, from `[happy-1]` to `[happy-7]`, `[boundary-1]` to `[boundary-3]`, `[unhappy-1]` to `[unhappy-3]` and `[concurrency-1]` to `[concurrency-3]`. The tests use `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, are all flat at the top level, and borrow the required variables from `env.test.ts` and the `createApp` setup from `routes.test.ts`.

**Some boundary cases go beyond the spec's examples.** Each one tests a rule the spec states:
- **Reads only one key:** a recording wrapper around `env` checks that `IMAGE_DIGEST` is the only key read, and that it is read exactly once.
- **Never changes `env`:** the same wrapper checks that nothing writes to `env`. A frozen `env` with spaces around the digest must still resolve to the trimmed digest.
- **No console output:** while the lookalike digests are being rejected, the console methods are swapped out and must not be called.
- **Default argument:** `resolveImageDigest(undefined)` falls back to `process.env`. Tests that touch `process.env.IMAGE_DIGEST` restore it afterwards.
- **No cache:** after one call has finished, a second call sees a new value in `env`.
- **Read at call time:** setting a digest after calling with an empty `env` still gives `undefined` for that call.

44 tests, in 1 file.

private.finalText:
I wrote the hidden suite in three files under `apps/api/test/hidden-image-digest/`:

- **`resolve-values.test.ts`** covers happy 1–5, boundary 1–3 and unhappy 1–3.
- **`concurrency.test.ts`** covers concurrency 1–3.
- **`existing-behaviour.test.ts`** covers happy 6–7 (`parseEnv`, `buildInfo` and `GET /version`).

`npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors. Against the current stub, all 110 tests fail on the `not implemented` error. I checked them against a straightforward correct implementation kept only in my scratchpad, and all 110 hidden tests plus the 44 public ones passed. Nothing in the repository changed outside the new folder apart from the `dist-test` build output that the required command produces.

**Shortcuts these tests catch that the public suite lets through:**
- **Reading the value at the wrong time:** IMAGE_DIGEST must already have been read by the time the call returns. A test cuts off access to `env` right after the call, so a late read fails. With 200 concurrent calls, each must read the key exactly once, which rules out sharing one result between calls.
- **Caching:** no cached `undefined` when calls start on an unset env, and no single result shared between different env objects.
- **Hardcoding:** 40+ computed sha256 digests (via `node:crypto`) plus DIGEST_B and padded variants, so code that only knows DIGEST_A fails.
- **Looser matching:** a multiline-flag regex (`garbage\n<digest>`), keeping only the first word or first line (`<digest> latest`, `<digest>\n<digest>`), lowercasing, adding `sha256:` to bare hex, taking the part after `@`, stripping quotes or a trailing NUL, a doubled prefix, sha512/sha384, 128 hex characters, a single uppercase character, and a 1 MB input.
- **Trimming only some whitespace:** one-sided padding, CR only, CRLF, mixed runs and 10,000-character runs.
- **Other inputs:** no `fetch` call even when `ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4` is set, frozen envs of every kind, envs left unchanged when the key is missing or `undefined`, and `process.env` left unchanged and never captured once at load.

I tried five such shortcut implementations. The hidden suite failed every one, and two of them (the multiline regex and stripping a trailing NUL) pass the whole public suite.

**Not tested because the spec leaves them open:** a value that isn't a string, an env that throws when read, a value inherited through the prototype, and whether `\v`, `\f` or Unicode spaces count as surrounding whitespace.

110 tests, in 3 files.

Open in the spec: none
